title: Canonical stage-cohomology comparison certificates
statement: Let P be a predicate on schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For abelian groups A and B, a morphism v:A→B has a stage-cohomology comparison certificate for P if it belongs to the following inductively generated class. Every isomorphism has a certificate. Composites and finite binary products of certified maps have certificates. For a scheme S with P(S), take any nonempty directed preorder I and inverse diagram of qcqs schemes with affine transitions [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a specified limiting cone T, and a coherent system F_i of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Its inverse-image transitions [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] satisfy the canonical identity and composition equations. Take a diagram G on T with specified isomorphisms to the pullbacks of F_i and their canonical transition formula, and a specified sheaf colimit L [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. In degree p, take a group diagram H with specified isomorphisms to H^p(F_i) [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], arrows conjugate to coefficient transition after cohomology pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], and a cocone B identified with H^p(L), whose legs are the canonical pullback and coefficient maps. If a supplied stage D_i0 is isomorphic to S, the canonical morphism colim H→B.pt has a certificate. This last constructor requires the scheme limit and sheaf colimit but no cohomology colimit proof. The definition is a proposition about supplied maps, with no chosen data.
